performance_optimizations.title: Implement route-level code splitting with React.lazy for Backoffice app
performance_optimizations.description: The backoffice app eagerly imports 30+ page components at startup (DashboardPage, ListingsPage, BookingsPage, etc.), creating a large initial bundle. Implementing React.lazy() for route components would split these into separate chunks loaded on demand.
performance_optimizations.rationale: apps/backoffice/src/App.tsx imports all page components at the top level, meaning the entire admin interface (~30 pages) loads upfront even though users typically access one page at a time. This significantly impacts Time to Interactive (TTI) and First Contentful Paint (FCP). The .cursorrules file recommends React.lazy() but it's not implemented.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: All 30+ route components loaded in initial bundle (~200-300KB compressed)
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~60-70% reduction in initial bundle size, TTI improvement of 1-2 seconds on slower connections
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Create lazy wrapper: `const DashboardPage = lazy(() => import('./routes/dashboard'))`
2. Wrap Routes in Suspense with loading fallback
3. Apply to all route components in backoffice/App.tsx
4. Add prefetching for likely navigation targets using `<link rel='prefetch'>`
5. Consider route grouping by role to optimize chunk loading
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Slightly slower navigation on first visit to each route; requires Suspense fallback UI; need to handle loading states gracefully

performance_optimizations.title: Dynamically import Mapbox-GL to reduce initial bundle by ~500KB
performance_optimizations.description: mapbox-gl (~500KB uncompressed, ~150KB gzipped) is bundled in @xala/ds package and loaded on every page, even those without maps. Moving map components to dynamic imports would eliminate this from the initial bundle.
performance_optimizations.rationale: The @xala/ds package includes mapbox-gl and react-map-gl as dependencies. These are used by ListingMap component but loaded universally. Most pages (dashboard, bookings, settings) don't need maps, yet users pay the bundle size cost on every page load.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: mapbox-gl adds ~500KB to vendor bundle, loaded on all pages
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~150KB gzipped reduction in initial bundle, ~500ms faster LCP on median connections
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Move mapbox-gl to peer/optional dependency in @xala/ds
2. Create lazy-loaded ListingMap wrapper:
   ```tsx
   const ListingMap = lazy(() => import('./ListingMap.impl'))
   ```
3. Export ListingMap with Suspense boundary built-in
4. Update apps to only load map chunk when map is visible
5. Consider using IntersectionObserver to defer map loading until in viewport
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Map will have brief loading state on first render; requires careful handling of map initialization; need to preload when user hovers over map tab

performance_optimizations.title: Add staleTime configuration to frequently-used SDK query hooks
performance_optimizations.description: Most React Query hooks in @digilist/client-sdk lack staleTime configuration, causing unnecessary refetches when components remount or focus returns to the window. Adding appropriate staleTime values would reduce API calls and improve perceived performance.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Hooks like useBookings, useRentalObjects, useOrganizations, and useDashboardStats refetch on every component mount (staleTime defaults to 0). Only useBookingModeConfig (60s) and useRecurringPreview (30s) have explicit staleTime. This causes redundant network requests when navigating between tabs or returning to previously-viewed pages.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: ~15 API calls on dashboard load, redundant fetches on tab switches
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~50% reduction in API calls, smoother navigation experience, reduced server load
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Users may see slightly stale data between refetches; need to balance freshness vs. network calls; consider invalidation strategy for mutations

performance_optimizations.title: Add Vite manual chunking strategy to backoffice app matching web app
performance_optimizations.description: The backoffice app's vite.config.ts lacks the manual chunking strategy implemented in the web app. Adding vendor-specific chunks for mapbox, react-query, SDK, and design system would improve caching and parallel loading.
performance_optimizations.rationale: apps/web/vite.config.ts splits vendors into: vendor-mapbox, vendor-query, vendor-sdk, vendor-ds, and vendor. apps/backoffice/vite.config.ts has no manualChunks configuration, resulting in a single large vendor bundle. This defeats browser caching when only SDK code changes and prevents parallel chunk loading.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: Single vendor chunk ~800KB; full re-download on any dependency update
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: Better cache utilization (70%+ cache hit rate), parallel loading of chunks, ~30% faster repeat visits
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: More HTTP requests initially (though HTTP/2 mitigates this); need to verify no circular dependency issues between chunks

performance_optimizations.title: Optimize design system barrel exports to improve tree-shaking
performance_optimizations.description: The @xala/ds package uses `export * from '@digdir/designsystemet-react'` which can import the entire designsystemet library even when only a few components are used. Explicit named exports would enable better tree-shaking.
performance_optimizations.rationale: packages/ds/src/index.ts re-exports everything from @digdir/designsystemet-react using `export *`. While modern bundlers handle this reasonably well, some components and their dependencies may be included unnecessarily. Apps only use a subset (~30-40 components) of the full library (~80+ components).
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: Full designsystemet library included (~100KB), many unused components bundled
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~20-30KB reduction in DS bundle size, better tree-shaking accuracy
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: More maintenance overhead to keep export list updated; may break apps if they use undocumented exports; need to verify all component dependencies are included

keyFindings: No route-level code splitting in backoffice (30+ eager imports)
mapbox-gl loaded on all pages despite limited map usage
SDK hooks lack staleTime causing redundant fetches
Backoffice missing web app's manual chunk strategy
Barrel exports may defeat tree-shaking for design system
